newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Illegal trade closes Yugo tobacco plant DIN-paper.
newsitem.headline: Illegal trade closes Yugo tobacco plant DIN-paper.

text.p: Booming illegal cigarette trade has forced Yugoslavia's biggest tobacco factory, Duvanska Industrija Nis (DIN), to close down for the next three weeks, the Belgrade newspaper Vecernje Novosti said on Monday.
"Promises of rigorous measures to clamp down on cigarette smuggling made by competent bodies in early March have not been fulfilled and the black market trade has actually picked up," the paper said.

As a result, DIN in March sold just 500 tonnes of cigarettes, of which barely 200 tonnes on the domestic market, while its stocks are huge, which is why it has been forced to temporarily halt its machines as of today, the report said.
No-one at DIN was immediately available for comment.

DIN called on the government for immediate intervention since tobacco factories in the country lost around 700 million dinars ($126 million) last year due to reduced sales of their products which are burdened by taxes on the local market.
Local producers face strict financial controls, while smuggled cigarettes are not subject to any taxes or customs duties.

Besides losses of income for the state budget, the grey economy has brought Yugoslav cigarette producers into great insolvency and is preventing them from carrying out their obligations towards suppliers, the state and employees, whose wages are paid with delays of up to several months.

According to the latest data of the Tobacco Fund, smuggled cigarettes account for nearly 83 percent of total sales in the country. The contraband mainly comes from neighbouring countries such as Bulgaria, Macedonia and Albania.
The Tobacco Fund last month said Serbia lost around 1.25 billion dinars from uncollected 1996 tax revenues due to the illegal ciragette trade.
Local producers sold slightly more than 7,000 tonnes of ciragettes in 1996, less than a third of the estimated annual consumption of 23,000 tonnes.
